Enterprise tier bypasses all limits\n\n### Interfaces to define (in quota.go):\n\n```go\n// QuotaRepository defines the persistence methods the quota checker needs.\ntype QuotaRepository interface {\n\tGetActiveSubscription(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID string) (*model.Subscription, error)\n\tCountKBsByOrg(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID string) (int, error)\n\tCountMembersByOrg(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID string) (int, error)\n\tGetVoiceUsageForPeriod(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID string, periodStart time.Time) (int, error)\n}\n\n// SubscriptionCache provides cached subscription lookups.\ntype SubscriptionCache interface {\n\tGet(ctx context.Context, orgID string) (*model.OrgSubscription, error)\n\tSet(ctx context.Context, orgID string, sub *model.OrgSubscription) error\n}\n\n// QuotaCheckerI is the interface for quota enforcement (used by services that need limit checks).\ntype QuotaCheckerI interface {\n\tCheckKBQuota(ctx context.Context, orgID string) error\n\tCheckSeatQuota(ctx context.Context, orgID string) error\n\tCheckVoiceMinuteQuota(ctx context.Context, orgID string) error\n\tGetConcurrentVoiceLimit(ctx context.Context, orgID string) int\n\tGetUsage(ctx context.Context, orgID string) (*model.UsageResponse, error)\n\tGetOrgSubscription(ctx context.Context, orgID string) (*model.OrgSubscription, error)\n}\n```\n\n### QuotaChecker struct:\n\n```go\ntype QuotaChecker struct {\n\trepo  QuotaRepository\n\tcache SubscriptionCache\n\tpool  *pgxpool.Pool\n\tplans map[string]model.Plan\n}\n```\n\n### Methods to implement:\n\n1. `NewQuotaChecker(repo, cache, pool)` — constructor, builds plans map from `model.DefaultPlans()`\n2. `GetOrgSubscription(ctx, orgID)` — check cache → DB fallback → cache result. Default to free plan if no subscription found. Use `db.WithOrgID` for DB access when pool is non-nil; call repo directly with nil tx when pool is nil (unit test path).\n3. `CheckKBQuota(ctx, orgID)` — get org subscription, return nil if unlimited, count KBs, return `apierror.NewPaymentRequired(...)` if at/over limit\n4. `CheckSeatQuota(ctx, orgID)` — same pattern for members vs `Plan.MaxUsers`\n5. `CheckVoiceMinuteQuota(ctx, orgID)` — same pattern for voice minutes vs `Plan.MaxVoiceMinutesMonthly`. Use subscription's `CurrentPeriodStart` for the billing period, or `time.Now().UTC().AddDate(0, -1, 0)` if no subscription.\n6. `GetConcurrentVoiceLimit(ctx, orgID)` — returns `Plan.MaxConcurrentVoiceSessions` (-1 for unlimited)\n7. `GetUsage(ctx, orgID)` — aggregate all usage counts into `model.UsageResponse`\n\n### ValkeySubscriptionCache:\n\n```go\ntype ValkeySubscriptionCache struct {\n\tclient redis.Cmdable\n\tttl    time.Duration\n}\n```\n\n- Key prefix: `raven:org_sub:`\n- TTL: 5 minutes\n- Uses JSON marshal/unmarshal\n- 200ms context timeout for Valkey calls\n- Returns (nil, nil) on cache miss\n\n### Important patterns:\n- **Fail-open**: On any DB/cache error, log warning and allow the request (default to free tier, don't block)\n- Use `db.WithOrgID(ctx, q.pool, orgID, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {...})` for all DB operations\n- Use `slog.ErrorContext`/`slog.WarnContext` for logging\n- Import `\"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/db\"` for `db.WithOrgID`\n- Import `\"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/pkg/apierror\"` for error types\n- Import `\"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/model\"` for model types\n\n### Tests to write (in quota_test.go):\n\nUse mock implementations of `QuotaRepository` and `SubscriptionCache`. Pass `nil` for pool (unit test path).\n\nTest cases:\n1. `TestCheckKBQuota_FreeAtLimit_Returns402` — no subscription (free tier), kbCount=3, expect 402 with limit=3\n2. `TestCheckKBQuota_EnterpriseBypass` — subscription with plan_enterprise, kbCount=999, expect nil error\n3. `TestCheckKBQuota_ProUnderLimit_Passes` — subscription with plan_pro, kbCount=10, expect nil error\n4. `TestCheckSeatQuota_FreeAtLimit_Returns402` — no subscription, memberCount=5, expect 402\n5. `TestCheckVoiceMinuteQuota_FreeAtLimit_Returns402` — no subscription, voiceUsage=3600 (60min in seconds), expect 402 with limit=60\n6. `TestCheckVoiceMinuteQuota_UnderLimit_Passes` — voiceUsage=1800 (30min), expect nil\n7. `TestGetConcurrentVoiceLimit_EnterpriseBypass` — returns -1\n\n## Context\n\n- Task 1 added `apierror.QuotaError` and `NewPaymentRequired(detail, limit)` \n- Task 2 added `model.OrgSubscription`, `model.DefaultFreeSubscription()`, `model.UsageResponse`, and `MaxVoiceMinutesMonthly` to `Plan`\n- Task 3 added `repository.BillingRepository` with `GetActiveSubscription`, `CountKBsByOrg`, `CountMembersByOrg`, `GetVoiceUsageForPeriod`\n- Free plan limits: MaxKBs=3, MaxUsers=5, MaxVoiceMinutesMonthly=60, MaxConcurrentVoiceSessions=1\n- Pro plan limits: MaxKBs=50, MaxUsers=25, MaxVoiceMinutesMonthly=1200, MaxConcurrentVoiceSessions=5\n- Enterprise: all -1 (unlimited)\n\n## Your Job\n\n1. 14	// BillingRepository handles database operations for subscriptions and payment events.
15	// All operations run inside a pgx.Tx with org_id set for RLS.
16	type BillingRepository struct {
17		pool *pgxpool.Pool
18	}

20	// NewBillingRepository creates a new BillingRepository.
21	func NewBillingRepository(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *BillingRepository {
22		return &BillingRepository{pool: pool}
23	}
24	
25	const (
26		sqlSubscriptionInsert = `
27			INSERT INTO subscriptions (org_id, plan_id, status, hyperswitch_subscription_id, current_period_start, current_period_end)
28			VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)
29			RETURNING id, org_id, plan_id, status, hyperswitch_subscription_id,
30			          current_period_start, current_period_end, created_at`
31	
32		sqlSubscriptionByID = `
33			SELECT id, org_id, plan_id, status, hyperswitch_subscription_id,
34			       current_period_start, current_period_end, created_at
35			FROM subscriptions
36			WHERE id = $1 AND org_id = $2`
37	
38		sqlSubscriptionByHyperswitchID = `
39			SELECT id, org_id, plan_id, status, hyperswitch_subscription_id,
40			       current_period_start, current_period_end, created_at
41			FROM subscriptions
42			WHERE hyperswitch_subscription_id = $1`
43	
44		sqlSubscriptionActiveByOrg = `
45			SELECT id, org_id, plan_id, status, hyperswitch_subscription_id,
46			       current_period_start, current_period_end, created_at
47			FROM subscriptions
48			WHERE org_id = $1 AND status IN ('active', 'trialing', 'past_due')
49			LIMIT 1`
50	
51		sqlSubscriptionUpdateStatus = `
52			UPDATE subscriptions SET status = $3
53			WHERE id = $1 AND org_id = $2
54			RETURNING id, org_id, plan_id, status, hyperswitch_subscription_id,
55			          current_period_start, current_period_end, created_at`
56	
57		sqlSubscriptionExtendPeriod = `
58			UPDATE subscriptions SET
59				status = 'active',
60				current_period_start = now(),
61				current_period_end   = now() + interval '1 month'
62			WHERE hyperswitch_subscription_id = $1
63			RETURNING id, org_id, plan_id, status, hyperswitch_subscription_id,
64			          current_period_start, current_period_end, created_at`
65	
66		sqlPaymentEventInsert = `
67			INSERT INTO payment_events (org_id, event_type, payment_id, status, raw_payload)
68			VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)
69			ON CONFLICT (payment_id, event_type) DO NOTHING
70			RETURNING id`
71	
72		sqlPaymentEventExists = `
73			SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM payment_events WHERE payment_id = $1 AND event_type = $2)`
74	)

76	func scanSubscription(row pgx.Row) (*model.Subscription, error) {
77		var s model.Subscription
78		err := row.Scan(
79			&s.ID,
80			&s.OrgID,
81			&s.PlanID,
82			&s.Status,
83			&s.HyperswitchSubscriptionID,
84			&s.CurrentPeriodStart,
85			&s.CurrentPeriodEnd,
86			&s.CreatedAt,
87		)
88		if err != nil {
89			return nil, err
90		}
91		return &s, nil
92	}
93	
94	// CreateSubscription inserts a new subscription and returns it with DB-assigned fields.
95	func (r *BillingRepository) CreateSubscription(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, sub *model.Subscription) (*model.Subscription, error) {
96		row := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlSubscriptionInsert,
97			sub.OrgID,
98			sub.PlanID,
99			sub.Status,
100			sub.HyperswitchSubscriptionID,
101			sub.CurrentPeriodStart,

103		)
104		result, err := scanSubscription(row)
105		if err != nil {
106			return nil, fmt.Errorf("BillingRepository.CreateSubscription: %w", err)
107		}
108		return result, nil
109	}

113		row := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlSubscriptionByID, subscriptionID, orgID)

139	func (r *BillingRepository) GetActiveSubscription(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID string) (*model.Subscription, error) {

153		row := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlSubscriptionUpdateStatus, subscriptionID, orgID, status)

161	// ExtendSubscriptionPeriod resets the billing period for a subscription identified
162	// by its Hyperswitch ID. Used when a recurring payment succeeds.
163	func (r *BillingRepository) ExtendSubscriptionPeriod(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, hyperswitchID string) (*model.Subscription, error) {
164		row := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlSubscriptionExtendPeriod, hyperswitchID)
165		s, err := scanSubscription(row)
166		if err != nil {
167			return nil, fmt.Errorf("BillingRepository.ExtendSubscriptionPeriod: %w", err)
168		}
169		return s, nil
170	}
171	
172	// InsertPaymentEvent records a webhook event for idempotency. Returns true if
173	// the row was inserted (i.e. the event is new), false if it already existed.
174	func (r *BillingRepository) InsertPaymentEvent(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID, eventType, paymentID, status string, rawPayload []byte) (bool, error) {
175		var id *string
176		err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlPaymentEventInsert, orgID, eventType, paymentID, status, rawPayload).Scan(&id)
177		if err != nil {
178			if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
179				// ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — duplicate event, already processed.
180				return false, nil
181			}
182			return false, fmt.Errorf("BillingRepository.InsertPaymentEvent: %w", err)
183		}
184		return true, nil
185	}
186	
187	// PaymentEventExists checks whether a payment event has already been processed.
188	func (r *BillingRepository) PaymentEventExists(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, paymentID, eventType string) (bool, error) {
189		var exists bool
190		if err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlPaymentEventExists, paymentID, eventType).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
191			return false, fmt.Errorf("BillingRepository.PaymentEventExists: %w", err)
192		}
193		return exists, nil
194	}

Returns true if\n// the row was inserted (i.e. the event is new), false if it already existed.\nfunc (r *BillingRepository) InsertPaymentEvent(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID, eventType, paymentID, status string, rawPayload []byte) (bool, error) {\n\tvar id *string\n\terr := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlPaymentEventInsert, orgID, eventType, paymentID, status, rawPayload).Scan(&id)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tif errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {\n\t\t\t// ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — duplicate event, already processed.\n\t\t\treturn false, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false, fmt.Errorf(\"BillingRepository.InsertPaymentEvent: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn true, nil\n}\n\n// PaymentEventExists checks whether a payment event has already been processed.\nfunc (r *BillingRepository) PaymentEventExists(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, paymentID, eventType string) (bool, error) {\n\tvar exists bool\n\tif err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlPaymentEventExists, paymentID, eventType).Scan(&exists); err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, fmt.Errorf(\"BillingRepository.PaymentEventExists: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn exists, nil\n}\n\n// CountKBsByOrg returns the number of active (non-archived) knowledge bases for an org.\nfunc (r *BillingRepository) CountKBsByOrg(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID string) (int, error) {\n\tvar count int\n\terr := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlCountKBsByOrg, orgID).Scan(&count)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn 0, fmt.Errorf(\"BillingRepository.CountKBsByOrg: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn count, nil\n}\n\n// CountMembersByOrg returns the number of distinct users across all workspaces in an org.\nfunc (r *BillingRepository) CountMembersByOrg(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID string) (int, error) {\n\tvar count int\n\terr := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlCountMembersByOrg, orgID).Scan(&count)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn 0, fmt.Errorf(\"BillingRepository.CountMembersByOrg: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn count, nil\n}\n\n// GetVoiceUsageForPeriod returns total voice duration (seconds) for an org since periodStart.\nfunc (r *BillingRepository) GetVoiceUsageForPeriod(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID string, periodStart time.Time) (int, error) {\n\tvar totalSeconds int\n\terr := tx.QueryRow(ctx, sqlVoiceUsageForPeriod, orgID, periodStart).Scan(&totalSeconds)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn 0, fmt.Errorf(\"BillingRepository.GetVoiceUsageForPeriod: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn totalSeconds, nil\n}\n"
}

package service

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"time"

	"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/model"
	"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/pkg/apierror"
)

// BillingRepository defines the persistence interface for billing operations.
type BillingRepository interface {
	CreateSubscription(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, sub *model.Subscription) (*model.Subscription, error)
	GetSubscriptionByID(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID, subscriptionID string) (*model.Subscription, error)
	GetSubscriptionByHyperswitchID(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, hsID string) (*model.Subscription, error)
	GetActiveSubscription(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID string) (*model.Subscription, error)
	UpdateSubscriptionStatus(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID, subscriptionID string, status model.SubscriptionStatus) (*model.Subscription, error)
	ExtendSubscriptionPeriod(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, hyperswitchID string) (*model.Subscription, error)
	InsertPaymentEvent(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orgID, eventType, paymentID, status string, rawPayload []byte) (bool, error)
}

// HyperswitchClient defines the interface for Hyperswitch API operations.
type HyperswitchClient interface {
	CreatePayment(ctx context.Context, req *hyperswitch.CreatePaymentRequest) (*hyperswitch.PaymentResponse, error)
	CancelPayment(ctx context.Context, paymentID string) error
}

// BillingService contains business logic for subscription and payment management
// via the Hyperswitch payment orchestration platform.

## Frontend Structure & Billing Implementation Report

### 1. Vue.js Frontend Structure

**Main Entry Point**: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/frontend/src/main.ts`
- Initializes Pinia (Vue state management)
- Initializes Keycloak authentication before mounting
- Uses PostHog for analytics with feature flags

**Directory Layout**:
```
frontend/src/
├── api/           # API client modules (individual service layers)
├── components/    # Reusable Vue components
├── composables/   # Composition API utilities
├── ee/           # Enterprise Edition features
├── layouts/      # Page layouts (AuthLayout, DefaultLayout)
├── pages/        # Page components (route views)
├── plugins/      # Vue plugins (PostHog)
├── router/       # Vue Router configuration
├── stores/       # Pinia stores (state management)
├── types/        # TypeScript type definitions
└── assets/       # Static assets
```

### 2. Router Structure

**File**: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/frontend/src/router/index.ts`
- Uses `createRouter` with web history mode
- Two main layouts:
  - `AuthLayout.vue` - for login & legal pages (no auth required)
  - `DefaultLayout.vue` - for authenticated pages (requires `meta.requiresAuth`)
- Route guard: `router.beforeEach()` checks `useAuthStore().isAuthenticated` and redirects to login if needed
- Currently **NO billing/settings routes** - issue #194 requires adding them

**Key Routes**:
- `/dashboard` - main app entry
- `/orgs/:orgId` - org detail page
- `/orgs/:orgId/workspaces` - workspace management
- `/orgs/:orgId/voice` - voice sessions
- `/orgs/:orgId/whatsapp/*` - WhatsApp integration
- `/api-keys`, `/llm-providers`, `/chatbot-config`, `/analytics` - settings pages

### 3. API Client Setup

**File**: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/frontend/src/api/client.ts`
- Simple fetch-based client with `getAuthHeaders()` (reads `auth_token` from localStorage)
- No axios, no interceptors currently
- Exposes `api` object with methods: `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`

**Per-Service API Modules** (`api/*.ts`):
- Each service file imports `useAuthStore()` and implements `authFetch(path, init)`
- Uses: `Authorization: Bearer ${auth.accessToken}` header
- Base URL: `import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL ?? '/api/v1'`
- Example: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/frontend/src/api/apikeys.ts` uses mock data (TODO comments for real API)

### 4. Pinia Store Structure

**File**: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/frontend/src/stores/auth.ts`
- Uses Keycloak JS SDK for OpenID Connect authentication
- Stores: `user`, `accessToken`, `initialized`
- Methods: `init()`, `login()`, `logout()`
- Auto-refreshes token 30s before expiry
- Integrates with PostHog for analytics identification

**Standard Store Pattern** (e.g., `apikeys.ts`, `workspaces.ts`):
```typescript
export const useMyStore = defineStore('my-store', () => {
  const items = ref([])
  const loading = ref(false)
  const error = ref<string | null>(null)
  
  async function fetchItems() {
    loading.value = true
    try {
      items.value = await listItemsAPI()
    } catch (e) {
      error.value = (e as Error).message
    } finally {
      loading.value = false
    }
  }
  
  return { items, loading, error, fetchItems }
})
```

### 5. Authentication Details

**Keycloak/OIDC Setup** (from `stores/auth.ts`):
- Config: `VITE_KEYCLOAK_URL`, `VITE_KEYCLOAK_REALM` (`'raven'`), `VITE_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID` (`'raven-admin'`)
- Token stored in localStorage as `auth_token`
- User info parsed from Keycloak JWT (`tokenParsed`):
  - `id` (from `sub` claim)
  - `email`
  - `username`
  - `orgId` (custom claim `org_id`)
  - `orgRole` (custom claim `org_role`)

### 6. Feature Flag System

**Implementation**: PostHog-based feature flags
- **File**: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/frontend/src/composables/useFeatureFlag.ts`
- **Composable**: `useFeatureFlag(flagName)` returns reactive `isEnabled` ref
- **Integration**: `/src/plugins/posthog.ts` handles PostHog initialization
  - Opt-in analytics (respects cookie consent)
  - Flag reload listeners dispatch `CustomEvent('posthog:flags-loaded')`
  - Automatic pageview tracking via router hook
- **Config**: `VITE_POSTHOG_API_KEY`, `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST`

### 7. Components & Layout

**DefaultLayout.vue**: 
- Sidebar navigation (icon-based on desktop, expandable on mobile)
- AppHeader (top bar)
- MobileTabBar (bottom navigation on mobile)
- ResponsiveLayout using `useMobile()` composable

**AppSidebar.vue**:
- Routes to: Dashboard, Voice Sessions, API Keys, LLM Providers, Chatbot Config, Analytics
- Mobile sidebar overlays with backdrop
- **No settings/billing menu items yet** - needs to be added for issue #194

**AppHeader.vue**:
- Profile/settings/logout placeholder (comment: "will open a dropdown with profile/settings/logout")

### 8. 402 Payment Required Error Handling

**Backend Implementation** (from git log & `pkg/apierror/apierror.go`):
- `QuotaError` struct extends `AppError` with `UpgradeRequired: bool` and `Limit: int` fields
- `NewPaymentRequired(detail string, limit int)` creates 402 responses

package service

import (
	"context"
	"regexp"
	"strings"

	"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/model"
	"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/repository"
	"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/pkg/apierror"
)

// OrgService contains business logic for organisation management.
type OrgService struct {
	repo *repository.OrgRepository
}

// NewOrgService creates a new OrgService.
func NewOrgService(repo *repository.OrgRepository) *OrgService {
	return &OrgService{repo: repo}
}

var slugRe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-z0-9]+`)

// toSlug converts a human-readable name to a URL-safe slug.
func toSlug(name string) string {
	s := strings.ToLower(name)
	s = slugRe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
	return strings.Trim(s, "-")
}

// Create validates the request, derives a slug, and persists a new organisation.
func (s *OrgService) Create(ctx context.Context, req model.CreateOrgRequest) (*model.Organization, error) {
	slug := toSlug(req.Name)
	if slug == "" {
		return nil, apierror.NewBadRequest("organisation name produces an empty slug")
	}
	org, err := s.repo.Create(ctx, req.Name, slug)
	if err != nil {
		// A unique-constraint violation means the slug is already taken.
		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unique") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "duplicate") {
			return nil, apierror.NewBadRequest("organisation slug already taken: " + slug)
		}
		return nil, apierror.NewInternal("failed to create organisation: " + err.Error())
	}
	return org, nil
}

// GetByID retrieves an active organisation by ID.
func (s *OrgService) GetByID(ctx context.Context, orgID string) (*model.Organization, error) {
	org, err := s.repo.GetByID(ctx, orgID)
	if err != nil {
		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "no rows") {
			return nil, apierror.NewNotFound("organisation not found")
		}
		return nil, apierror.NewInternal("failed to fetch organisation: " + err.Error())
	}
	return org, nil
}

// Update applies a partial update to an organisation.
func (s *OrgService) Update(ctx context.Context, orgID string, req model.UpdateOrgRequest) (*model.Organization, error) {
	org, err := s.repo.Update(ctx, orgID, req.Name, req.Settings)
	if err != nil {
		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "no rows") {
			return nil, apierror.NewNotFound("organisation not found")
		}
		return nil, apierror.NewInternal("failed to update organisation: " + err.Error())
	}
	return org, nil
}

// Delete soft-deletes an organisation by setting its status to 'deactivated'.
func (s *OrgService) Delete(ctx context.Context, orgID string) error {
	if err := s.repo.SoftDelete(ctx, orgID); err != nil {
		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "not found") {
			return apierror.NewNotFound("organisation not found")
		}
		return apierror.NewInternal("failed to delete organisation: " + err.Error())
	}
	return nil
}

})

router.beforeEach(async (to) => {
  if (to.meta.requiresAuth) {
    const auth = useAuthStore()
    if (!auth.isAuthenticated) {
      auth.login()
      return false
    }
  }

  if (to.name === 'login') {
    const auth = useAuthStore()
    if (auth.isAuthenticated) {
      return { name: 'dashboard' }
    }
  }
})

export default router

package repository

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"
	"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/model"
)

// OrgRepository handles database operations for organisations.
// It does NOT enforce RLS itself — callers must use db.WithOrgID when operating
// inside a tenant context. Org creation and admin reads run without RLS.
type OrgRepository struct {
	pool *pgxpool.Pool
}

// NewOrgRepository creates a new OrgRepository backed by pool.
func NewOrgRepository(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *OrgRepository {
	return &OrgRepository{pool: pool}
}

const orgColumns = `id, name, slug, status, settings, COALESCE(keycloak_realm, '') AS keycloak_realm, created_at, updated_at`

func scanOrg(row pgx.Row) (*model.Organization, error) {
	var org model.Organization
	err := row.Scan(
		&org.ID,
		&org.Name,
		&org.Slug,
		&org.Status,
		&org.Settings,
		&org.KeycloakRealm,
		&org.CreatedAt,
		&org.UpdatedAt,
	)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &org, nil
}

// Create inserts a new organisation and returns the persisted record.
func (r *OrgRepository) Create(ctx context.Context, name, slug string) (*model.Organization, error) {
	row := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx,
		`INSERT INTO organizations (name, slug)
		 VALUES ($1, $2)
		 RETURNING `+orgColumns,
		name, slug,
	)
	org, err := scanOrg(row)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("OrgRepository.Create: %w", err)
	}
	return org, nil
}

// GetByID fetches a non-deactivated organisation by its UUID.
func (r *OrgRepository) GetByID(ctx context.Context, orgID string) (*model.Organization, error) {
	row := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx,
		`SELECT `+orgColumns+`
		 FROM organizations
		 WHERE id = $1 AND status != 'deactivated'`,
		orgID,
	)
	org, err := scanOrg(row)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("OrgRepository.GetByID: %w", err)
	}
	return org, nil
}

// Update applies partial updates (name and/or settings) to an organisation.
func (r *OrgRepository) Update(ctx context.Context, orgID string, name *string, settings map[string]any) (*model.Organization, error) {
	row := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx,
		`UPDATE organizations
		 SET
		   name     = COALESCE($2, name),
		   settings = CASE WHEN $3::jsonb IS NOT NULL THEN $3::jsonb ELSE settings END

import { defineStore } from 'pinia'
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
import Keycloak from 'keycloak-js'
import { usePostHog } from '../plugins/posthog'

export interface AuthUser {
  id: string
  email: string
  username: string
  orgId: string
  orgRole: string
}

const keycloak = new Keycloak({
  url: import.meta.env.VITE_KEYCLOAK_URL ?? 'http://localhost:8080',
  realm: import.meta.env.VITE_KEYCLOAK_REALM ?? 'raven',
  clientId: import.meta.env.VITE_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID ?? 'raven-admin',
})

export const useAuthStore = defineStore('auth', () => {
  const user = ref<AuthUser | null>(null)
  const accessToken = ref<string | null>(null)
  const initialized = ref(false)

  const isAuthenticated = computed(() => initialized.value && !!accessToken.value)

  async function init(): Promise<void> {
    try {
      const authenticated = await keycloak.init({
        onLoad: 'check-sso',
        pkceMethod: 'S256',
        silentCheckSsoRedirectUri: window.location.origin + '/silent-check-sso.html',
      })
      if (authenticated) {
        _syncFromKeycloak()
        // Auto-refresh token 30s before expiry
        setInterval(() => keycloak.updateToken(30), 60_000)
      }
    } catch {
      // Keycloak unavailable — proceed as unauthenticated
    } finally {
      initialized.value = true
    }
  }

  function login(): void {
    keycloak.login({ redirectUri: window.location.origin + '/dashboard' })
  }

  function logout(): void {
    // Reset PostHog identity before logging out.
    const { reset: resetPostHog } = usePostHog()
    resetPostHog()
    keycloak.logout({ redirectUri: window.location.origin + '/' })
  }

  function _syncFromKeycloak(): void {
    const p = keycloak.tokenParsed as Record<string, unknown>
    accessToken.value = keycloak.token ?? null
    user.value = {
      id: p['sub'] as string,
      email: p['email'] as string,
      username: p['preferred_username'] as string,
      orgId: p['org_id'] as string,
      orgRole: p['org_role'] as string,
    }

    // Identify the authenticated user in PostHog for analytics.
    const { identify } = usePostHog()
    identify(user.value.id, {
      email: user.value.email,
      username: user.value.username,
      org_id: user.value.orgId,
      org_role: user.value.orgRole,
    })
  }

  return { user, accessToken, isAuthenticated, initialized, init, login, logout }
})

# RAG Pipeline Approaches for Raven

**Date:** 2026-03-27
**Status:** Research draft -- no code written

---

## Context

Raven is a multi-tenant knowledge-base platform. Documents are parsed by LiteParse (text/JSON with bounding boxes), web content is scraped as markdown, embeddings are stored in PostgreSQL + pgvector, and full-text search uses ParadeDB (BM25). Three interaction modes -- chatbot, voice agent, and WebRTC -- query the same retrieval pipeline.

This document presents three approaches to the RAG pipeline, covering chunking, embedding models, LLM selection, knowledge graph, retrieval strategy, and orchestration.

---

## Approach A: Pragmatic Hybrid (Recommended Starting Point)

> **Philosophy:** Ship fast with managed services, minimize operational complexity, and rely on proven hybrid retrieval without a knowledge graph.

### Components

| Layer | Choice | Rationale |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| **Chunking** | Recursive character splitting with document-structure awareness | LiteParse outputs bounding boxes and structural hints (headings, tables, lists). Use these to define chunk boundaries, falling back to recursive splitting (e.g., 512 tokens, 50-token overlap) within structurally flat sections. Preserve heading hierarchy as chunk metadata. |
| **Embedding model** | OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` (1536d) | Best cost/performance ratio for a managed service. Supports `dimensions` parameter to reduce to 512d or 256d if needed for storage savings. Matryoshka-style truncation. No GPU infra required. |
| **LLM** | Multi-provider: Anthropic Claude (primary), OpenAI GPT-4o (fallback) | Claude Sonnet for chat and synthesis; Claude Haiku for low-latency voice agent responses. GPT-4o as a fallback provider for resilience. Provider abstraction via a thin routing layer. |
| **Knowledge graph** | **Skip KG** -- pure vector + BM25 hybrid | Adding a knowledge graph adds significant complexity (entity extraction, schema maintenance, graph queries). For the initial version, hybrid search with good chunking and metadata filtering covers the vast majority of knowledge-base queries. KG can be layered in later (see Approach C). |
| **Retrieval** | Hybrid vector + BM25 via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) | Two parallel queries: (1) pgvector cosine similarity, (2) ParadeDB BM25 `@@@` operator. Results merged via RRF (`k=60`). Top-N candidates passed to a reranker. |
| **Reranking** | Cohere Rerank v3 | Applied to the top 20-30 RRF results. Reranks to top 5-8 for the LLM context window. Significant relevance improvement for minimal latency cost (~100ms). |
| **Pipeline orchestration** | Custom (lightweight) | A thin Python service with clearly defined stages: chunk -> embed -> store -> retrieve -> rerank -> generate. No framework overhead. Each stage is a function with typed inputs/outputs. Easy to test, easy to swap components. |

### Pros
- **Fastest to production.** No graph DB, no self-hosted models, no framework lock-in.
- **Low operational burden.** Managed embedding and reranking APIs. Single Postgres instance for vectors + BM25 + relational data.
- **Good baseline quality.** Hybrid search + reranking consistently outperforms pure vector search in benchmarks (MTEB, BEIR).
- **Multi-tenant friendly.** Tenant isolation via Postgres row-level security or schema-per-tenant; no separate infra per tenant.

### Cons
- **API cost scales with volume.** Embedding and reranking API calls have per-token/per-query costs.
- **Vendor dependency.** Embedding model is OpenAI; reranking is Cohere; LLM is Anthropic/OpenAI. Three external dependencies.
- **No deep relational understanding.** Without a knowledge graph, the system cannot answer multi-hop relational queries well (e.g., "What products does the supplier of component X also provide?").
- **RRF fusion is manual.** Until ParadeDB ships native hybrid search, the fusion logic lives in application code.

### Chunking Detail

```
Document (LiteParse output)
  |
  +-- Extract structural elements (headings, tables, lists, paragraphs)
  |
  +-- For each section (heading-bounded):
  |     |
  |     +-- If section fits in one chunk (< 512 tokens): keep as-is
  |     |
  |     +-- If section is too large: recursive split on paragraph -> sentence boundaries
  |           with 50-token overlap
  |
  +-- Tables: each table becomes its own chunk with the table caption/heading as prefix
  |
  +-- Metadata per chunk:
===
# ParadeDB + pgvector Research Summary

**Date:** 2026-03-27
**Status:** Research only - no code written

---

## 1. What is ParadeDB?

ParadeDB is a **PostgreSQL extension** (`pg_search`) that brings Elastic-quality full-text search and analytics directly inside Postgres. It is NOT a fork; it installs as an extension on any Postgres 15+ instance.

**Core extension:** `pg_search` -- introduces a custom **BM25 index** type built on an LSM tree architecture, with each segment containing both an inverted index (for text search) and a columnar index (for fast aggregates).

**Key features already shipping (v0.22.3):**
- Full-text search with BM25 scoring
- 12+ tokenizers, 20+ language support
- Top-K retrieval, highlighting, faceted search
- Filtering, aggregates (bucket, metrics, facets) with columnar storage
- JOIN pushdown (beta) for INNER/SEMI/ANTI joins
- Custom operators (`@@@`) and custom scan nodes with parallelization

**What is NOT yet shipping:**
- Vector search (coming soon -- on roadmap)
- Hybrid search combining BM25 + vector similarity (coming soon -- on roadmap)

### How it differs from plain PostgreSQL + pgvector

ParadeDB and pgvector solve **different problems**:

| Aspect | pgvector | ParadeDB (pg_search) |
|--------|----------|---------------------|
| Primary purpose | Vector similarity search (embeddings) | Full-text search (BM25), analytics |
| Index type | HNSW, IVFFlat | BM25 (LSM tree with inverted + columnar) |
| Query type | Nearest-neighbor on embeddings | Text search, filtering, aggregates |
| Scoring | Cosine/L2/inner product distance | BM25 relevance scoring |
| Hybrid search | Not natively (manual RRF needed) | Planned: combine BM25 + vector in single query |

**They are complementary, not competing.** For a knowledge base, you would use:
- **pgvector** for semantic similarity via embeddings
- **ParadeDB** for keyword/full-text search with BM25

Here's what Phase 2 / M9 looks like based on the confirmed features and existing research:

---

**M9: Intelligence & Retention**

Three pillars:

### 1. Semantic Response Cache
The biggest one — minimize LLM API costs by catching similar questions before they hit the LLM.
- Cache Q&A pairs with their embeddings in Postgres (pgvector)
- On incoming query: cosine similarity check against cache first (~5ms vs ~800ms LLM call)
- If similarity ≥ threshold (e.g. 0.92): serve cached answer, adapted to user's tone via a small local model (the "in-DB LLM" concept)
- If miss: hit LLM, store result in cache for future hits
- Per-KB cache with TTL + manual invalidation on document updates
- Metrics: cache hit rate, tokens saved, cost avoided

### 2. Conversation Email Summaries
- After a voice/chat session ends, generate a summary via LLM
- Email it to the user with a "Resume conversation" deep-link
- Provider: AWS SES (already in your infra research)
- Configurable: users can opt-in/out per workspace

### 3. Cross-Channel Conversation Memory
- Link sessions across chat, voice, and WebRTC by user identity (Keycloak `sub`)
- Store conversation history in Postgres with PostHog event tracking
- RAG pipeline gets prior context injected (last N turns) for continuity
- PostHog cohorts: identify power users, drop-off points, channel preferences

---

prompt includes the last N turns of conversation history.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\nIncoming message (any channel)\n    │\n    ▼\nGo API: resolve user identity (Keycloak sub → user_id)\n    │\n    ▼\nFetch last N conversation turns from conversation_sessions\n    │\n    ▼\nInject as conversation_history into AI worker request\n    │\n    ▼\nAI worker: prepend history to system prompt context\n    │\n    ▼\nPostHog: track message_sent event with session/channel metadata\n```\n\n## Tasks\n\n### Database\n- [ ] Migration: `conversation_sessions` table (shared with #257 — coordinate)\n  ```sql\n user_id     TEXT NOT NULL,  -- Keycloak sub claim\n    channel     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (channel IN ('chat', 'voice', 'webrtc')),\n    messages    JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',  -- [{role, content, ts}]\n    started_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\n    ended_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,\n    summary     TEXT  -- populated by #257\n  );\n  CREATE INDEX ON conversation_sessions (kb_id, user_id, started_at DESC);\n  ```\n\n### Go API\n- [ ] `ConversationRepository`: `CreateSession`, `AppendMessage`, `EndSession`, `GetRecentByUser(kb_id, user_id, limit int) []Session`\n- [ ] Middleware: on authenticated chat/voice requests, resolve `user_id` from JWT `sub` claim and attach to context\n- [ ] Pass `conversation_history` (last 5 turns) in the gRPC/HTTP request to the AI worker\n- [ ] `GET /api/v1/orgs/:orgId/knowledge-bases/:kbId/conversations` — paginated session history for the current user\n- [ ] `GET /api/v1/orgs/:orgId/knowledge-bases/:kbId/conversations/:sessionId` — full session transcript\n\n### Python AI Worker\n- [ ] Accept `conversation_history: [{role, content}]` in chat/voice request\n- [ ] Prepend history to system prompt: \"Previous conversation context:\\n{history}\\n\\nNow answer:\"\n- [ ] Limit to last 5 turns (≈ 1500 tokens) to stay within context budget\n\n### PostHog Tracking\n- [ ] Go API: emit PostHog events server-side using PostHog Go SDK\n  - `session_started` — `{channel, kb_id, org_id}`\n  - `message_sent` — `{channel, kb_id, is_returning_user, history_turns_injected}`\n  - `session_ended` — `{channel, kb_id, message_count, duration_seconds}`\n- [ ] PostHog `distinct_id` = Keycloak `sub` (stable across channels)\n- [ ] PostHog group: `org_id` (for org-level analytics)\n\n### Frontend\n- [ ] KB detail page: \"Recent conversations\" section listing the user's last 5 sessions with date, channel icon, and message count\n- [ ] Click on a session → full transcript view\n- [ ] Returning user greeting in chat widget: \"Welcome back! Last time you asked about [last session topic].\"\n\n### Observability\n- [ ] OpenObserve: sessions per day per channel, avg session length, returning user rate\n- [ ] PostHog funnel: session_started → message_sent (×3) → session_ended (measures engagement depth)\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n- Returning user's last 5 turns are injected into the AI context within 50ms (DB query + serialization)\n- PostHog receives `session_started` within 200ms of session creation\n- Conversation history visible in KB detail page within 1s of session end\n- No cross-user or cross-org history leakage (RLS enforced on `conversation_sessions`)\n- Chat widget shows returning user greeting on second+ visit to same KB\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | python3 -c \"import sys,json; i=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Created issue #{i[\\\"number\\\"]}: {i[\\\"title\\\"]}')\"",

### CI workflow
# CI workflow

name: Go CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'cmd/**'
      - 'internal/**'
      - 'pkg/**'
      - 'tests/**'
      - 'go.mod'
      - 'go.sum'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'cmd/**'
      - 'internal/**'
      - 'pkg/**'
      - 'tests/**'
      - 'go.mod'
      - 'go.sum'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    name: Build & Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version: '1.26.2'
          cache: true

      - run: go mod download

      - name: Install eBPF build tools
        run: sudo apt-get install -y clang llvm libbpf-dev linux-tools-$(uname -r) || sudo apt-get install -y clang llvm libbpf-dev

      - name: Pre-pull testcontainers image
        run: docker pull pgvector/pgvector:pg17

      - run: CGO_ENABLED=1 go build ./cmd/api

      - run: go test -race -timeout 30m -coverprofile=coverage.txt ./...
        env:
          TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED: "true"

      - run: go test -race -run '^TestMigrationsUpAndDown$' ./migrations/...
        env:
          TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED: "true"

      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v6
        with:
          files: coverage.txt
          fail_ci_if_error: false

### Raven — Claude Code Instructions > Pull Request Workflow
## Pull Request Workflow

After creating a PR with `gh pr create`, **always** immediately queue it for auto-merge:

```bash
gh pr merge <PR_NUMBER> --auto --squash
```

This queues the PR to squash-merge automatically once all CI checks pass. Do not wait for CI — enqueue immediately after creation.

21	
22	## What is Raven?
23	
24	Raven is a self-hostable, multi-tenant knowledge base platform that lets organizations ingest documents and web content, then query them through AI-powered channels -- an embeddable chatbot, a real-time voice agent, and WhatsApp. It combines hybrid retrieval (vector search + BM25), BYOK LLM support, and a modular architecture designed for both cloud and edge deployment.
25	
26	The platform is organized around a clear hierarchy: **Organizations** (tenant boundaries) contain **Workspaces** (operational sub-units), which contain **Knowledge Bases** (collections of documents and web sources). Each layer enforces data isolation through PostgreSQL Row-Level Security, Keycloak-based authentication, and API middleware.
27	
28	Raven is built for teams that need a production-grade RAG platform without vendor lock-in. Bring your own LLM keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere), deploy on a cloud VM or a Raspberry Pi, and own your data end to end.
29	
30	## Key Features
31	
32	- **Multi-tenant by design** -- organization-level data isolation with RLS, per-tenant billing, and role-based access control
33	- **Embeddable chatbot** -- drop-in `<raven-chat>` web component with SSE streaming and domain-scoped API keys
34	- **Voice agent** -- real-time voice interface via LiveKit Agents with STT/TTS pipeline
35	- **WebRTC and WhatsApp** -- browser-based and WhatsApp Business Calling API integration
36	- **BYOK LLM** -- bring your own API keys for Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Cohere, or self-hosted models
37	- **Hybrid search** -- pgvector cosine similarity + BM25 full-text search with Reciprocal Rank Fusion
38	- **Self-hostable** -- single Docker Compose deployment with no external SaaS dependencies required
39	- **Edge-deployable** -- Go API compiles to a ~25 MB ARM64 binary; run the API on a Raspberry Pi with a remote AI worker
40	
41	## Architecture Overview
42	
43	Raven uses a **two-process architecture**: a Go API server handles HTTP routing, authentication, and orchestration, while a Python AI worker handles all ML/AI workloads (embedding, RAG queries, document parsing, web scraping). The two communicate over gRPC, with Valkey (Redis-compatible) as the async job queue.
44	
45	PostgreSQL serves as the single source of truth -- storing relational data, vector embeddings (pgvector), and full-text search indexes. A Vue.js SPA provides the admin dashboard, and Keycloak handles identity management.
46	
47	## Tech Stack
48	
49	| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
50	|-------|-----------|---------|
51	| **API Server** | Go + Gin | REST API, JWT validation, tenant routing, SSE streaming |
52	| **AI Worker** | Python + gRPC | RAG queries, embeddings, document parsing, web scraping |
53	| **Database** | PostgreSQL 18 + pgvector | Relational data, vector search, BM25 full-text |
54	| **Frontend** | Vue.js 3 + Tailwind CSS | Admin dashboard (SPA, mobile-first, PWA-capable) |
55	| **Chatbot Widget** | Web Component | Embeddable `<raven-chat>` element |
56	| **Auth** | Keycloak | OIDC/OAuth2, user management, multi-tenant realms |
57	| **Job Queue** | Valkey (Redis fork) | Async document processing, caching, rate limiting |
58	| **Object Storage** | SeaweedFS | S3-compatible file storage (Apache 2.0) |
59	| **Voice** | LiveKit Server + Agents | WebRTC SFU, STT/LLM/TTS voice pipeline |
60	| **Reverse Proxy** | Traefik | Auto-TLS, routing, security headers |
61	
62	## Quick Start / Deployment
63	
64	> **Coming Soon** -- The Docker Compose deployment guide is currently in progress. Check back for updates or watch this repository for releases.
65	
66	```bash
67	# Planned usage (not yet available):
68	git clone https://github.com/user/raven.git
69	cd raven
70	cp .env.example .env
71	docker compose up -d
72	```
73	
74	## Roadmap
75	
76	Development is organized into five phases. See the full [design specification](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-27-raven-platform-design-final.md) for details.
77	
78	| Phase | Scope | Target |
79	|-------|-------|--------|
80	| **Phase 1** | MVP -- embeddable chatbot, document ingestion, hybrid search, admin dashboard | 8-12 weeks |
81	| **Phase 2** | Voice agent (LiveKit), smart response caching, email notifications | +4-6 weeks |
82	| **Phase 3** | WebRTC / WhatsApp Business Calling API integration | +4-6 weeks |
83	| **Phase 4** | Knowledge graph (Neo4j, multi-hop queries) | Future |
84	| **Phase 5** | Cloud managed offering, multi-region, SOC 2 | Future |
85	
86	## Contributing
87	
88	Contributions are welcome. Please open an issue to discuss proposed changes before submitting a pull request.
89	
90	- Browse [open issues](../../issues) for tasks and bug reports
91	- See the [design specification](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-27-raven-platform-design-final.md) for architectural context

This prevents duplicate effort and lets us align on approach before you invest time writing code.\n\n## Branch Naming\n\n| Prefix | When |\n|--------|------|\n| `feat/` | New feature |\n| `fix/` | Bug fix |\n| `refactor/` | Code restructure, no behaviour change |\n| `ci/` | CI/CD changes |\n| `chore/` | Tooling, deps, config |\n| `deps/` | Dependency bumps |\n\nExample: `feat/semantic-cache`, `fix/voice-session-timeout`\n\n## Commit Style\n\n- Use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, etc.\n- Keep the subject line under 72 characters\n- No AI attribution trailers (`Co-Authored-By:` etc.)\n\n## Pull Request Workflow\n\n1. Branch off `main`\n2. Make your changes with passing tests and lint\n3. Open a PR against `main`\n4. Immediately queue auto-merge after creation:\n\n```bash\ngh pr create --title \"...\" --body \"...\" --base main\ngh pr merge <PR_NUMBER> --auto --squash\n```\n\nPRs squash-merge only — no regular merge, no rebase-merge.\n\n## Quality Gates\n\nAll of these must pass **locally** before pushing. CI will reject if they don't.\n\n### Go (backend)\n\n```bash\n# Build\ngo build ./...\n\n# Tests (including integration tests — needs Docker)\ngo test -race -timeout 30m ./...\n\n# Lint\ngolangci-lint run\n```\n\n### Python (AI worker)\n\n```bash\ncd ai-worker\nruff check .\nruff format --check .\npytest\n```\n\n### Frontend\n\n```bash\ncd frontend\nnpm run lint          # ESLint\nnpx tsc --noEmit      # TypeScript check\nnpm run test:unit     # Vitest unit tests\nnpm run build         # Production build (catches type errors vite misses)\n```\n\n### End-to-End (Playwright)\n\nE2E tests run against a live stack. See [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) for setup.\n\n```bash\ncd frontend\nnpm run test:e2e\n```\n\n## Code Style\n\n### Go\n\n- Follow standard Go conventions (`gofmt`, `golangci-lint`)\n- Handler → Service → Repository layering — no direct DB access from handlers\n- Return `*apierror.AppError` at service boundaries; let `apierror.ErrorHandler()` middleware render the response\n- Use `pgx.Tx` with `db.WithOrgID` for all tenant-scoped DB operations (RLS enforcement)\n- Wrap errors: `fmt.Errorf(\"ServiceName.MethodName: %w\", err)`\n\n### Python\n\n- `ruff` for formatting and linting (configured in `pyproject.toml`)\n- Type hints on all public functions\n- `structlog` for structured logging — no bare `print()`\n\n### Vue / TypeScript\n\n- Composition API with `<script setup>` — no Options API\n- Pinia for all shared state\n- Tailwind CSS only — no additional CSS frameworks\n- `useAuthStore()` for auth; `useFeatureFlag()` for PostHog feature flags\n\n## Testing Expectations\n\n- **Unit tests**: every new function with logic gets a test\n- **Integration tests** (Go): use `testutil.NewTestDB()` — it spins up a real Postgres via testcontainers\n- **No mocking the database** in integration tests — we got burned by mock/prod divergence before\n- **Playwright E2E**: cover the happy path for any new user-facing flow\n\n## Database Migrations\n\nMigrations live in `migrations/` and use [goose](https://github.com/pressly/goose).\n\n```bash\n# Apply all pending migrations\nmake migrate-up\n\n# Roll back one migration\nmake migrate-down\n```\n\nRules:\n- Never edit an existing migration file after it has been merged to `main`\n- Every new table needs RLS policies — see existing migrations for the pattern\n- Column renames = new migration with `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN`\n\n## Never\n\n- Push directly to `main`\n- Use `--no-verify` to skip hooks\n- Amend published commits\n- Force-push to `main`\n"
}

  "content": "# Development Guide\n\nEverything you need to run Raven locally, understand the codebase, and work with the AI-assisted development toolchain.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n1. [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)\n2. [Local Setup (Docker Compose)](#local-setup-docker-compose)\n3. [Local Setup (Without Docker)](#local-setup-without-docker)\n4. [Go API Server](#go-api-server)\n5. [Python AI Worker](#python-ai-worker)\n6. [Vue.js Frontend](#vuejs-frontend)\n7. [Database Migrations](#database-migrations)\n8. [Running Tests](#running-tests)\n9. [Make Targets](#make-targets)\n10. [AI-Assisted Development with MCP Tools](#ai-assisted-development-with-mcp-tools)\n\n---\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n| Tool | Version | Install |\n|------|---------|---------|\n| Docker + Docker Compose | Latest | [docs.docker.com](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) |\n| Go | 1.26+ | [go.dev/dl](https://go.dev/dl/) |\n| Python | 3.12+ | [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/) |\n| Node.js | LTS (22+) | [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/) |\n| `golangci-lint` | Latest | `brew install golangci-lint` |\n| `goose` | Latest | `go install github.com/pressly/goose/v3/cmd/goose@latest` |\n| `air` | Latest | `go install github.com/air-verse/air@latest` (hot reload) |\n| `ruff` | Latest | `pip install ruff` |\n| Playwright | — | `npx playwright install` (after `npm install`) |\n\n---\n\n## Local Setup (Docker Compose)\n\nThe fastest path — everything runs in containers.\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven.git\ncd Raven\n\n# Copy and configure environment\ncp .env.example .env\n# Edit .env — at minimum set:\n#   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY (for LLM calls)\n#   RAVEN_KEYCLOAK_ISSUERURL (default: http://localhost:8080/realms/raven)\n\n# Start all services\ndocker compose up -d\n\n# Watch logs\ndocker compose logs -f go-api python-worker\n```\n\nServices and their ports:\n\n| Service | URL | Notes |\n|---------|-----|-------|\n| Admin dashboard | http://localhost:3000 | Vue.js frontend (served by Vite in dev mode) |\n| Go API | http://localhost:8080 | REST API + SSE |\n| Keycloak | http://localhost:8081 | Identity provider |\n| PostgreSQL | localhost:5432 | pgvector + ParadeDB |\n| Valkey | localhost:6379 | Redis-compatible cache/queue |\n| SeaweedFS Filer | http://localhost:8888 | Object storage |\n| OpenObserve | http://localhost:5080 | Logs, metrics, traces |\n| Traefik dashboard | http://localhost:8090 | Reverse proxy (dev only) |\n\n**First-time Keycloak setup:**\n\n```bash\n# Provision the raven realm automatically\ncurl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/internal/provision-realm \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -H \"X-Internal-Key: $(grep RAVEN_INTERNAL_API_KEY .env | cut -d= -f2)\" \\\n  -d '{\"realm\": \"raven\"}'\n\n# Then log in to Keycloak admin at http://localhost:8081\n# Default admin creds are in your .env (KEYCLOAK_ADMIN / KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD)\n# Create a user in the raven realm with role org_admin\n```\n\n---\n\n## Local Setup (Without Docker)\n\nRun each service natively for faster iteration.\n\n### 1. Start infrastructure only\n\n```bash\n# Start only the backing services (Postgres, Valkey, Keycloak, SeaweedFS)\ndocker compose up -d postgres valkey keycloak seaweedfs-master seaweedfs-volume seaweedfs-filer\n```\n\n### 2. Apply database migrations\n\n```bash\nexport DATABASE_URL=\"postgresql://raven:changeme@localhost:5432/raven?sslmode=disable\"\nmake migrate-up\n```\n\n### 3. Go API (with hot reload)\n\n```bash\nexport $(cat .env | grep -v '#' | xargs)\nmake dev       # uses `air` for hot reload\n# OR\nmake run       # no hot reload\n```\n\n### 4. Python AI Worker\n\n```bash\ncd ai-worker\npython -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate\npip install -e \".[dev]\"\n\n# Start the gRPC worker\npython -m raven_worker.server\n```\n\n### 5. Frontend\n\n```bash\ncd frontend\nnpm install\nnpm run dev    # Vite dev server at http://localhost:3000\n```\n\n---\n\n## Go API Server\n\n**Entry point:** `cmd/api/main.go`\n\n**Package layout:**\n\n```\ninternal/\n├── config/       — Viper config, env bindings\n├── handler/      — Gin HTTP handlers (one file per resource)\n├── service/      — Business logic (handler → service → repository)\n├── repository/   — pgx database queries (SQL constants + scan functions)\n├── middleware/   — JWT auth, RLS org context, rate limiting, tier enforcement\n├── model/        — Shared types (structs for DB rows, API requests/responses)\n├── integration/  — External service clients (Keycloak admin, etc.)\n├── jobs/         — Asynq background task handlers\n└── ee/           — Enterprise Edition feature stubs\npkg/\n├── apierror/     — AppError, QuotaError, error middleware\n└── db/           — pgx helpers (WithOrgID for RLS transactions)\n```\n\n**Adding a new endpoint:**\n\n1. Add SQL constants + scan function to `internal/repository/`\n2. Add business logic method to `internal/service/`\n3. Add Gin handler to `internal/handler/`\n4. Wire route in `cmd/api/main.go`\n\n**Error handling convention:**\n\n```go\n// In service layer — return typed apierror\nreturn nil, apierror.NewNotFound(\"knowledge base not found\")\n\n// In handler — use c.Error() + c.Abort(), let middleware render\nif err != nil {\n    _ = c.Error(err)\n    c.Abort()\n    return\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Python AI Worker\n\n**Entry point:** `ai-worker/raven_worker/server.py`\n\n**gRPC service definitions:** `ai-worker/proto/`\n\n**Key modules:**\n\n```\nraven_worker/\n├── server.py          — gRPC server startup\n├── servicer.py        — gRPC method implementations\n├── rag/               — Retrieval-augmented generation pipeline\n│   ├── retrieval.py   — pgvector + BM25 hybrid search with RRF\n│   ├── reranker.py    — Cohere reranking\n│   └── generator.py   — LLM call + streaming\n├── processors/        — Document parsing (PDF, HTML, markdown)\n├── embedding/         — Embedding provider abstraction (OpenAI, Cohere)\n└── voice/             — LiveKit voice agent integration\n```\n\n**Running tests:**\n\n```bash\ncd ai-worker\npytest                        # all tests\npytest tests/test_rag_service.py -v    # specific module\npytest tests/smoke/ -v -m smoke        # smoke tests (need live API keys)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Vue.js Frontend\n\n**Entry point:** `frontend/src/main.ts`\n\n**Directory layout:**\n\n```\nfrontend/src/\n├── api/          — API modules (one per backend resource, typed fetch wrappers)\n├── components/   — Reusable Vue components\n├── composables/  — Composition API utilities (useFeatureFlag, useOnboarding, etc.)\n├── layouts/      — Page layouts (AuthLayout, DefaultLayout)\n├── pages/        — Route views (one directory per feature area)\n├── router/       — Vue Router configuration\n├── stores/       — Pinia stores (auth, billing, etc.)\n└── types/        — Shared TypeScript type definitions\n```\n\n**Adding a new page:**\n\n1. Create `frontend/src/api/<resource>.ts` — typed `authFetch` wrappers\n2. Create `frontend/src/stores/<resource>.ts` — Pinia store\n3. Create `frontend/src/pages/<feature>/YourPage.vue`\n4. Add route to `frontend/src/router/index.ts`\n\n**Feature flags** (PostHog):\n\n```typescript\nimport { useFeatureFlag } from '../composables/useFeatureFlag'\nconst { isEnabled } = useFeatureFlag('your_flag_name')\n```\n\n**402 / quota errors** — handled globally via the shared `authFetch` in `src/api/utils.ts`, which calls `useBillingStore().flagQuotaExceeded()` automatically. No per-page handling needed.\n\n---\n\n## Database Migrations\n\nMigrations use [goose](https://github.com/pressly/goose) and live in `migrations/`.\n\n```bash\nmake migrate-up      # apply all pending\nmake migrate-down    # roll back one step\n```\n\n**Writing a migration:**\n\n```sql\n-- migrations/00042_add_query_cache.sql\n-- +goose Up\nCREATE TABLE query_cache (\n    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    org_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),\n    ...\n);\n-- RLS is required on every new tenant-scoped table\nALTER TABLE query_cache ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nCREATE POLICY query_cache_isolation ON query_cache\n    USING (org_id = current_setting('app.org_id')::uuid);\n\n-- +goose Down\nDROP TABLE query_cache;\n```\n\nRules:\n- Never edit a migration that has been merged to `main`\n- Every tenant-scoped table needs an RLS policy\n- Use `gen_random_uuid()` for primary keys\n\n---\n\n## Running Tests\n\n### Go\n\n```bash\ngo test ./...                          # all tests\ngo test -race -timeout 30m ./...       # with race detector (same as CI)\ngo test ./internal/service/... -v      # specific package\ngo test -run TestQuotaChecker ./...    # specific test\n```\n\nIntegration tests spin up a real Postgres via [testcontainers](https://testcontainers.com/). Docker must be running.\n\n```bash\n# Skip integration tests if no Docker\ngo test -short ./...\n```\n\n### Python\n\n```bash\ncd ai-worker\npytest                   # all\npytest -x                # stop on first failure\npytest -k \"test_rag\"     # filter by name\nruff check .             # lint\nruff format --check .    # format check\n```\n\n### Frontend\n\n```bash\ncd frontend\nnpm run test:unit        # Vitest (fast, no browser)\nnpm run test:e2e         # Playwright (needs running stack)\nnpx tsc --noEmit         # TypeScript check without building\nnpm run build            # full production build (catches more type errors)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Make Targets\n\n```bash\nmake build        # go build -o bin/api ./cmd/api\nmake run          # go run ./cmd/api\nmake dev          # air (hot reload)\nmake test         # go test ./...\nmake lint         # golangci-lint run\nmake migrate-up   # goose up\nmake migrate-down # goose down\nmake swagger      # regenerate docs/swagger from source\nmake proto        # regenerate gRPC stubs from proto files\n```\n\n---\n\n## AI-Assisted Development with MCP Tools\n\nThis project is developed with Claude Code, which has a suite of MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools wired in. If you're contributing using Claude Code, here's how to use them effectively.\n\n### Local Semantic Search — `context-mode`\n\nThe most important tool for exploring the codebase. Instead of grepping for strings, index everything and query semantically.\n\n**Index the codebase and search in one call:**\n\n```\nctx_batch_execute(\n  commands=[\n    {\"label\": \"Handler files\", \"command\": \"ls internal/handler/\"},\n    {\"label\": \"Service layer\", \"command\": \"cat internal/service/quota.go\"},\n    {\"label\": \"Config struct\", \"command\": \"grep -A 20 'type Config struct' internal/config/config.go\"},\n  ],\n  queries=[\n    \"quota checker service interface methods\",\n    \"how RLS org_id is set in transactions\",\n    \"billing payment intent handler\",\n  ]\n)\n```\n\n**Follow-up searches** (after an initial index):\n\n```\nctx_search(queries=[\n  \"pgx transaction WithOrgID pattern\",\n  \"apierror QuotaError 402 response\",\n])\n```\n\n**When to use it:**\n- Before writing any new code — understand the existing pattern first\n- When you don't know which file contains something\n- When `grep` would return too many results to read\n\n### Symbolic Code Navigation — `serena`\n\nNavigate by symbol, not by file. Great for understanding how things connect.\n\n```\n# Find a symbol and its usages\nserena.find_symbol(\"QuotaChecker\", include_body=true)\nserena.find_referencing_symbols(\"NewQuotaChecker\")\n\n# Get an overview of all symbols in a file\nserena.get_symbols_overview(\"internal/service/quota.go\")\n\n# Safe rename across the codebase\nserena.rename_symbol(\"OldName\", \"NewName\", relative_path=\"internal/service/quota.go\")\n```\n\n### Library Documentation — `context7`\n\nFetch accurate, up-to-date docs for any library instead of relying on training data.\n\n```\n# Always resolve the library ID first\ncontext7.resolve-library-id(\"pgx v5 postgres go\")\n# → /jackc/pgx\n\ncontext7.query-docs(\n  library_id=\"/jackc/pgx\",\n  query=\"how to use pgx.Tx QueryRow and scan results\"\n)\n```\n\nUse this whenever you're working with: pgx, gin, pinia, vue-router, keycloak-js, livekit, asynq, goose, testcontainers, vitest, playwright.\n\n### GitHub Operations — `mcp__github`\n\n```\n# Read an issue with full spec\nmcp__github.issue_read(method=\"get\", owner=\"ravencloak-org\", repo=\"Raven\", issue_number=256)\n\n# Read a PR's diff\nmcp__github.pull_request_read(method=\"get_diff\", ...)\n\n# Add a review comment\nmcp__github.pull_request_review_write(...)\n```\n\n### Browser Automation — `claude-in-chrome`\n\nFor verifying frontend behaviour without manual clicking.\n\n```\ntabs_context_mcp()          # always start here — see what's open\nnavigate(url=\"http://localhost:3000/billing\")\nfind(description=\"Upgrade button\")\njavascript_tool(code=\"document.querySelector('.usage-bar').style.width\")\nread_console_messages(pattern=\"\\\\[billing\\\\]\")\n```\n\n### Git Worktrees — standard pattern for this repo\n\nEvery feature is developed in an isolated worktree, not on the main working tree.\n\n```bash\n# Create a worktree for a new feature\ngit worktree add .worktrees/feat-my-feature -b feat/my-feature\n\n# Work inside it\ncd .worktrees/feat-my-feature\n\n# Clean up after merge\ngit worktree remove .worktrees/feat-my-feature\n```\n\nWorktrees are gitignored. Never commit the `.worktrees/` directory.\n\n### Parallel Agents for Independent Tasks\n\nWhen multiple files need to change independently (e.g. backend model + frontend component), dispatch subagents in parallel rather than working sequentially. Each agent gets a fresh context and works in the same worktree.\n\nSee the [superpowers skills](docs/superpowers/) for the full workflow: `writing-plans` → `subagent-driven-development` → `finishing-a-development-branch`.\n"
}

  "content": "# Raven Frontend\n\nVue.js 3 admin dashboard for the Raven platform. Mobile-first, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript.\n\n## Tech Stack\n\n- **Vue 3** — Composition API + `<script setup>`\n- **Pinia** — state management\n- **Vue Router** — client-side routing\n- **Tailwind CSS** — utility-first styling\n- **TypeScript** — strict mode\n- **Vite** — build tool\n- **Vitest** — unit tests\n- **Playwright** — end-to-end tests\n- **keycloak-js** — OIDC authentication\n\n## Getting Started\n\n```bash\nnpm install\nnpm run dev       # http://localhost:3000\n```\n\nRequires the Go API and Keycloak running. Easiest way:\n\n```bash\n# From repo root\ndocker compose up -d postgres valkey keycloak go-api\n```\n\nThen set your `.env` in the repo root (copy `.env.example`). Vite proxies `/api/v1` to `localhost:8080` in dev.\n\n## Environment Variables\n\nVite env vars are prefixed with `VITE_`. Copy `frontend/.env.example` if it exists, otherwise set:\n\n```bash\nVITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/api/v1\nVITE_KEYCLOAK_URL=http://localhost:8081\nVITE_KEYCLOAK_REALM=raven\nVITE_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID=raven-admin\nVITE_POSTHOG_API_KEY=         # leave empty to disable analytics\nVITE_HYPERSWITCH_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=  # only needed for billing flow\n```\n\n## Scripts\n\n```bash\nnpm run dev          # Vite dev server with HMR\nnpm run build        # Production build (vue-tsc + vite)\nnpm run preview      # Preview production build locally\nnpm run lint         # ESLint\nnpm run lint:fix     # ESLint with auto-fix\nnpm run format       # Prettier\nnpm run test:unit    # Vitest (fast, no browser)\nnpm run test:e2e     # Playwright (requires running stack)\nnpm run test         # unit + e2e\n```\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\nsrc/\n├── api/            # Typed fetch wrappers (one file per backend resource)\n│   ├── utils.ts    # Shared authFetch with 402 interceptor\n│   ├── billing.ts\n│   ├── knowledge-bases.ts\n│   └── ...\n├── components/     # Reusable components\n│   ├── AppSidebar.vue\n│   ├── AppHeader.vue\n│   ├── UsageBar.vue\n│   ├── PlanCard.vue\n│   ├── UpgradePromptBanner.vue\n│   └── ...\n├── composables/    # Composition API utilities\n│   ├── useFeatureFlag.ts   # PostHog feature flags\n│   ├── useOnboarding.ts    # First-run wizard state\n│   └── useMobile.ts\n├── layouts/\n│   ├── DefaultLayout.vue   # Authenticated pages (sidebar + header)\n│   └── AuthLayout.vue      # Login / legal pages\n├── pages/          # Route views (mirrored in router/index.ts)\n│   ├── billing/\n│   ├── knowledge-bases/\n│   ├── onboarding/\n│   ├── voice/\n│   └── ...\n├── router/\n│   └── index.ts    # All routes + beforeEach guard\n├── stores/         # Pinia stores\n│   ├── auth.ts     # Keycloak session, user identity\n│   ├── billing.ts  # Subscription, plans, usage, quota flag\n│   └── ...\n└── types/          # Shared TypeScript interfaces\n```\n\n## Authentication\n\nAuth is handled by `stores/auth.ts` using `keycloak-js`. On app init, Keycloak checks for an existing SSO session silently. Unauthenticated users are redirected to Keycloak login.\n\nThe JWT contains custom claims set by the Keycloak `raven-org` client scope:\n- `org_id` — the user's organisation UUID\n- `org_role` — `org_admin` or `org_member`\n\nAccess token is available as `useAuthStore().accessToken` and is automatically included by `authFetch`.\n\n## Feature Flags\n\nPostHog feature flags gate optional features (e.g. billing UI):\n\n```typescript\nimport { useFeatureFlag } from '../composables/useFeatureFlag'\n\nconst { isEnabled: billingEnabled } = useFeatureFlag('billing_enabled')\n```\n\nLeave `VITE_POSTHOG_API_KEY` empty during local development — all flags default to `false`, which safely hides billing/premium UI.\n\n## Adding a New Page\n\n1. `src/api/<resource>.ts` — API functions using `authFetch` from `./utils`\n2. `src/stores/<resource>.ts` — Pinia store (copy the pattern from `stores/billing.ts`)\n3. `src/pages/<feature>/YourPage.vue` — Vue SFC with `<script setup>`\n4. Add route in `src/router/index.ts` inside the `DefaultLayout` children\n5. Add nav item to `src/components/AppSidebar.vue` if needed\n\n## Testing\n\nUnit tests use Vitest and live alongside the source (`*.spec.ts` or in `tests/unit/`).\n\nE2E tests use Playwright and live in `e2e/`. They require a running stack:\n\n```bash\n# Start everything\ndocker compose up -d\n\n# Run E2E\nnpm run test:e2e\n\n# Run a specific spec\nnpx playwright test e2e/billing/billing.spec.ts --headed\n```\n"
}

> AGENT

The pipeline is in `.github/workflows/pages.yml`. Here's the current state:

**Workflow:** `Deploy Frontend to Cloudflare Pages`
- Triggers on pushes to `main` (and PRs) when `frontend/**` changes
- Builds with Node 22, runs lint, then `npm run build` with production env vars
- Deploys via `cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3` to project `raven-frontend`

**Deployment gate (line 64):**
```yaml
if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN != ''
```
Deploy only fires on merge to `main` — PRs get a build/lint check but no deploy.

**Required secrets/vars to wire up:**

| Name | Type | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | Secret | Wrangler auth — deploy is skipped if absent |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | Var | CF account to deploy into |
| `VITE_API_URL` | Var | Defaults to `https://api.ravencloak.org` |
| `VITE_KEYCLOAK_URL` | Var | Defaults to `https://auth.ravencloak.org` |
| `VITE_LIVEKIT_URL` | Var | Optional, defaults to empty |

**Current risk:** If `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` isn't set in the repo secrets, the deploy step silently skips — the workflow still "passes" but nothing gets pushed to Cloudflare Pages. Have you set that secret yet? If not, that's why nothing shows up at `https://raven-frontend.pages.dev` (or whatever the CF Pages URL is).

1	# Raven — EC2 server deployment
2	#
3	# Runs on a secondary Docker daemon (hidden from default docker ps).
4	# Cloudflare Tunnel handles all inbound traffic — no ports exposed to the internet.
5	#
6	# Usage:
7	#   DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/raven/docker.sock \
8	#   docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml --env-file .env.server up -d
9	
10	services:
11	  # ─── Go API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
12	  go-api:
13	    image: ${GO_API_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/go-api:latest}
14	    # Bind to loopback only — cloudflared reaches it, internet cannot.
15	    ports:
16	      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
17	    env_file: .env.server
18	    depends_on:
19	      postgres:
20	        condition: service_healthy
21	      valkey:
22	        condition: service_healthy
23	      keycloak:
24	        condition: service_started
25	    healthcheck:
26	      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:8080/healthz"]
27	      interval: 10s
28	      timeout: 5s
29	      retries: 5
30	      start_period: 15s
31	    networks:
32	      - raven-net
33	    restart: unless-stopped
34	
35	  # ─── Python AI Worker (gRPC) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
36	  python-worker:
37	    image: ${PYTHON_WORKER_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/python-worker:latest}
38	    env_file: .env.server
39	    environment:
40	      RAVEN_MEMORY_DIR: /var/raven/memories
41	    volumes:
42	      - raven-memories:/var/raven/memories
43	    depends_on:
44	      postgres:
45	        condition: service_healthy
46	      valkey:
47	        condition: service_healthy
48	    networks:
49	      - raven-net
50	    restart: unless-stopped
51	    # No external ports — go-api reaches it via Docker network on :50051
52	
53	  # ─── PostgreSQL + pgvector ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
54	  postgres:
55	    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg18
56	    environment:
57	      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-raven}
58	      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-raven}
59	      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?POSTGRES_PASSWORD is required}
60	    volumes:
61	      - pg-data:/var/lib/postgresql
62	      - ../../deploy/postgres/init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql:ro
63	    healthcheck:
64	      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-raven} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-raven}"]
65	      interval: 5s
66	      timeout: 5s
67	      retries: 5
68	    networks:
69	      - raven-net
70	    restart: unless-stopped
71	    # No external port — only reachable inside raven-net
72	
73	  # ─── Valkey ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
74	  valkey:
75	    image: valkey/valkey:8.1-alpine
76	    command: ["valkey-server", "--maxmemory", "512mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru", "--save", "60", "1"]
77	    volumes:

1	# Cloudflare Tunnel configuration for Raven
2	# Place at: /etc/cloudflared/config.yml
3	#
4	# Setup steps:
5	#   1. cloudflared tunnel login
6	#   2. cloudflared tunnel create raven
7	#   3. Replace TUNNEL_ID below with the UUID from step 2
8	#   4. cloudflared tunnel route dns raven ${RAVEN_DOMAIN}
9	#   5. cloudflared tunnel route dns raven auth.${RAVEN_DOMAIN}
10	#
11	# Or use a Zero Trust token instead (see setup.sh --token option).
12	
13	tunnel: TUNNEL_ID
14	credentials-file: /etc/cloudflared/TUNNEL_ID.json
15	
16	# No TLS origin — Keycloak and go-api serve plain HTTP internally.
17	# Cloudflare handles TLS at the edge.
18	originRequest:
19	  noTLSVerify: false
20	  connectTimeout: 10s
21	  tcpKeepAlive: 30s
22	  keepAliveTimeout: 90s
23	  keepAliveConnections: 100
24	
25	ingress:
26	  # Keycloak auth — must come before the catch-all
27	  - hostname: "${RAVEN_DOMAIN}"
28	    path: /auth
29	    service: http://localhost:8180
30	    originRequest:
31	      httpHostHeader: "${RAVEN_DOMAIN}"
32	
33	  # Go API (handles /api/*, /healthz)
34	  - hostname: "${RAVEN_DOMAIN}"
35	    service: http://localhost:8080
36	    originRequest:
37	      httpHostHeader: "${RAVEN_DOMAIN}"
38	
39	  # Catch-all (required by cloudflared)
40	  - service: http_status:404
41

> AGENT

The 502 + `nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu)` fingerprint tells the whole story — that's Ubuntu's system nginx package, not a Docker container. Here's what's happening:

**Root cause:** The frontend was never deployed to Cloudflare Pages. The Cloudflare Pages deploy step in `pages.yml:64` is gated on `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN != ''` — if that secret isn't set in GitHub, the step silently skips and nothing ever gets published.

Meanwhile, the Cloudflare Tunnel config (`cloudflared-config.yml`) has **no frontend route at all** — it only covers `/auth` → Keycloak (8180) and everything else → Go API (8080). There's also no frontend container in `docker-compose.server.yml`. So requests to your root domain fall through to whatever nginx is installed on the host OS, which has no backend to proxy to — hence 502.

**Two things need to happen:**

**1. Set the Cloudflare Pages secrets in GitHub**

Go to repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions and add:

| Name | Where to get it |
|------|----------------|
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | Cloudflare dashboard → My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token → "Edit Cloudflare Workers" template |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` (var, not secret) | Cloudflare dashboard → right sidebar |

Then create the Pages project once manually:
```bash
npx wrangler pages project create raven-frontend
```

After that, the next push to `main` that touches `frontend/**` will auto-deploy.

**2. Add a frontend route to the Cloudflare Tunnel**

The tunnel config needs to know where to send the frontend. Since CF Pages is a separate domain, the tunnel should route the main domain's `/` to the Pages URL. But the simpler approach for self-hosted: serve the built frontend from the EC2 directly via a lightweight nginx container and add a route.

Do you want me to:
- **a)** Add a frontend nginx container to `docker-compose.server.yml` + add its route to `cloudflared-config.yml` (fully self-hosted, no CF Pages dependency)
- **b)** Just document the `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` setup so the existing CF Pages workflow kicks in (intended architecture)
- **c)** Both — self-hosted as fallback, CF Pages as primary

| `dash.ravencloak.org` | Glance :8085 |

Full picture now. Here's what's actually in Cloudflare DNS:

**Root cause of 502:** `ravencloak.org` has two A records pointing to `15.197.148.33` and `3.33.130.190` — those are unrelated AWS IPs (likely old GoDaddy parking/placeholder records), not your EC2. Cloudflare proxies to those → 502.

**All current DNS records:**

| Name | Type | Target | Status |
|------|------|--------|--------|
| `ravencloak.org` | A | `15.197.148.33` / `3.33.130.190` | **Broken — wrong IPs** |
| `www.ravencloak.org` | CNAME | `ravencloak.org` | Broken (inherits root) |
| `api.ravencloak.org` | CNAME | tunnel | ✅ |
| `auth.ravencloak.org` | CNAME | tunnel | ✅ |

| `raven.ravencloak.org` | CNAME | different tunnel | Personal |
| `kos.ravencloak.org` | CNAME | different tunnel | Personal |

Fix: delete the broken A records, add `app.ravencloak.org` → your tunnel, and point the root domain to the tunnel too. Doing it now:

```json
{
  "code": "async () => {\n  const zoneId = \"29ab17874953f5c8538f67928e3bc617\";\n  const tunnelCname = \"f8371625-0249-4097-88be-9cf1df34db4a.cfargotunnel.com\";\n\n  // Get all records to find IDs for the broken A records\n  const records = await cloudflare.request({ method: \"GET\", path: `/zones/${zoneId}/dns_records`, query: { per_page: \"100\" } });\n\n  // Delete the two broken A records for ravencloak.org\n  const aRecords = records.result.filter(r => r.name === \"ravencloak.org\" && r.type === \"A\");\n  const deleteResults = await Promise.all(aRecords.map(r =>\n    cloudflare.request({ method: \"DELETE\", path: `/zones/${zoneId}/dns_records/${r.id}` })\n  ));\n\n  // Add app.ravencloak.org → tunnel\n  const addApp = await cloudflare.request({\n    method: \"POST\",\n    path: `/zones/${zoneId}/dns_records`,\n    body: { type: \"CNAME\", name: \"app\", content: tunnelCname, proxied: true, ttl: 1 }\n  });\n\n  // Add ravencloak.org → tunnel (CNAME flattening at apex)\n  const addRoot = await cloudflare.request({\n    method: \"POST\",\n    path: `/zones/${zoneId}/dns_records`,\n    body: { type: \"CNAME\", name: \"ravencloak.org\", content: tunnelCname, proxied: true, ttl: 1 }\n  });\n\n  return {\n    deleted: deleteResults.map(r => ({ success: r.success })),\n    app_added: { success: addApp.success, name: addApp.result?.name },\n    root_added: { success: addRoot.success, name: addRoot.result?.name }\n  };\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

PR ravencloak-org/Raven#264 queued. Once CI passes, the frontend Docker image will be built and pushed to GHCR.

For the DNS — you need to make 4 changes in the Cloudflare dashboard. Go to **dash.cloudflare.com → ravencloak.org → DNS → Records**:

**Delete these 2 A records** (the broken GoDaddy parking IPs):
| Type | Name | Value |
|------|------|-------|
| A | `ravencloak.org` | `15.197.148.33` |
| A | `ravencloak.org` | `3.33.130.190` |

**Add these 2 CNAME records** (both proxied ☁️):
| Type | Name | Value |
|------|------|-------|
| CNAME | `ravencloak.org` | `f8371625-0249-4097-88be-9cf1df34db4a.cfargotunnel.com` |
| CNAME | `app` | `f8371625-0249-4097-88be-9cf1df34db4a.cfargotunnel.com` |

Once those DNS changes are saved and PR #264 merges, pull the new image on the server:

```bash
ssh ubuntu@ec2-65-0-85-115.ap-south-1.compute.amazonaws.com \
  "cd /opt/raven && docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml pull frontend && docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml up -d frontend"
```

After that, `ravencloak.org`, `www.ravencloak.org`, and `app.ravencloak.org` will all serve the Vue SPA.

## MVP Launch — v0.2.0

This release marks the completion of the MVP Launch milestone, delivering the full Raven platform.

### What's new since v0.1.0 (Milestone 1)

**Mobile-first UI**
- Bottom tab bar navigation with 44px touch targets (#221)
- Table-to-card views for all list pages on mobile (#222)
- Full-screen responsive modals and bottom-sheet confirms (#223)
- Form adaptations with proper touch sizing (#224)
- Playwright mobile viewport E2E tests (Pixel 7 profile) (#225)

**Billing & Subscriptions**
- Hyperswitch + Razorpay payment integration (#192)
- Subscription enforcement — plan limit checks and feature gates on all quota-sensitive endpoints (#193)
- Billing and subscription management UI at /settings/billing (#194)

**Tenant Onboarding**
- Keycloak realm auto-provisioning via internal API (#197)
- 5-step onboarding wizard for new tenants (Welcome → KB → LLM → Test → Done)
- First-login redirect guard in router

**Observability**
- OpenObserve log aggregation + OTEL metrics wired (#198)
- OTel log exporter (otelslog bridge + otlploggrpc) restored (#235)

**Test suite**
- Full Go backend unit + integration test suite (#207)
- EE tests: WAF, licensing, webhooks HMAC, audit log (#230)
- Integration tests: migration correctness, gRPC fault injection, SSE streaming, webhook delivery (#231)
- Playwright E2E tests for all critical flows (#225)
- Python AI worker test suite

**Fixes & chores**
- RLS REVOKE cleanup in test fixtures (#232)
- testutil.NewTestDB migrations path hardening (#233)
- Webhook retry/dead-letter integration tests (#236)
- E2E secrets documentation (#238)
- Dependency rationale documented in go.mod (#239)
- Dashboard JSON files restored (#240)
- CodeRabbit review fixes across all PRs

### Docker deployment

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven.git
cd Raven
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env with your credentials
docker compose up -d
```
